events.s: Russia's Defence Ministry said it destroyed 1,214 Ukrainian drones across 19 regions, and Moscow's mayor said 613 flew toward the Moscow region. Three airports restricted flights and debris fell at a Sterlitamak chemical site. A separate strike on the Taman substation caused power outages across occupied Crimea.

events.h: Putin says Russia ready for war with Europe but does not want one
events.s: After calls with Finnish and Norwegian leaders, Putin said there would be no winners in a Russia-Europe war and that Moscow wants to avoid a Hormuz-style crisis in the Baltic. Denmark and Sweden publicly rebuked the Finland-Norway call.

events.h: Hormuz disruption forces energy scramble: QatarEnergy buys LNG, EU releases oil
events.s: QatarEnergy plans overseas LNG purchases and signed a deal with Woodside as force majeure on Hormuz shipping continues. EU states pledged to release 42.6 million barrels of oil, and EU energy prices are at four-year highs.
events.t: Higher energy prices and supply disruption weigh on Türkiye's import bill and its role as a transit corridor.

events.h: Netanyahu and Likud allege Arab-party election fraud; police and Shin Bet push back
events.s: Netanyahu accused Arab parties of foreign-backed election theft after his coalition lost its majority. Eisenkot accused him of an organised campaign to delegitimise the result. A senior police official and Shin Bet said fraud complaints were fewer than in past elections and the probe does not implicate a group of voters.

events.h: Israeli election seen raising prospect of attack on Iran; Iran meddling alleged
events.s: The National reads the Israeli results as raising the prospect of a new Israeli attack on Iran, and Ahmad Tibi claims Netanyahu plans war on Iran after the US midterms. Iranian analysts say a weakened Netanyahu is unlikely to change Israel's Iran policy. Reports also allege Iranian cyber and recruitment efforts aimed at Israel's election and the US midterms.

events.h: Ankara hosts 13th Organization of Turkic States summit; Aliyev sends FM instead
events.s: Foreign ministers met under Hakan Fidan ahead of the 29-30 October summit. Erdoğan spoke of Turkic unity and a 'Century of Türkiye', and Kyrgyz President Japarov received a Turkic World order. Aliyev skipped the summit and sent Foreign Minister Bayramov amid tensions over Türkiye's criticism of headscarf restrictions.
events.t: The summit showcases Ankara's Turkic leadership, but Azerbaijan's low-level attendance exposes friction with a key partner.

events.h: Türkiye and Uzbekistan sign five agreements including defence
events.s: Erdoğan and Mirziyoyev signed five bilateral agreements covering trade, investment, mining, transport, social security and defence. Türkiye aims to lift trade from $3.1 billion in 2025 to $5 billion, and a customs data protocol was also signed.
events.t: Deepens economic and defence ties in Central Asia.

events.h: Fidan to attend G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta
events.s: Hakan Fidan will attend the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta on 30-31 October to discuss regional crises and energy security. He is expected to press for more international pressure on Israel.
events.t: A chance for Ankara to engage Washington directly and push its line on Israel and regional crises.

events.h: Temporary Oleshky ceasefire holds as humanitarian convoy prepares to enter
events.s: Russia and Ukraine have observed a halt to hostilities around occupied Oleshky since 27 October, and sappers have cleared routes. A Ukraine-US-Russia delegation reached the aid hub ahead of the planned delivery, with residents allowed to leave. Zelensky said Russia was still striking civilians elsewhere.

events.h: Ukrainian Neptune missiles destroy two Russian Su-34 jets at Marinovka airfield
events.s: Ukraine's Navy said Neptune missiles destroyed two Su-34 bombers at Marinovka airfield in Volgograd Oblast. Zelensky also cited a hit on an Iskander launcher, and intelligence puts Su-34 losses at 43.

events.h: NATO pushes Patriot interceptors for Ukraine as US delays PAC-3 deliveries
events.s: NATO's deputy secretary general urged allies to transfer PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors from stockpiles to Ukraine. Partners fear the White House will not approve interceptors before the US congressional vote. PAC-3 deliveries are reportedly delayed while PAC-2s arrive through PURL.

events.h: European Commission opens over €20 billion in defence funds, urges joint procurement
events.s: The Commission invited member states to use about $23.7 billion in defence funds and apply for SAFE loans for joint procurement and Ukraine support.
events.t: EU defence funding rules and procurement preference shape Türkiye's access to European defence markets.

events.h: Israel tightens siege of Hebron as thousands displaced
events.s: Israeli forces have besieged and raided Hebron for a seventh day, with demolitions and over 3,300 people forced from their homes. The IDF may scale back its presence after evacuating thousands, with Netanyahu possibly more flexible after the election.

events.h: Israeli strikes in Gaza continue despite ceasefire
events.s: Israeli strikes killed several Palestinians, including at an Economy Ministry post in al-Mawasi, and damaged a UN warehouse. Over 21,000 patients await evacuation for treatment.
events.t: Türkiye is positioning itself as Gaza aid provider and critic of Israeli ceasefire violations.

events.h: SDF-Damascus integration advances amid Afrin return disputes and US oil takeover
events.s: Syrian officials agreed final steps to merge Kobani and Rojava universities. Ilham Ahmed said armed groups in Afrin hinder displaced residents' return. US firm HKN plans to double output at northeastern fields taken from Kurdish-run operations, and UN rights chief Türk pledged minority protection support.
events.t: The pace and terms of SDF integration affect Ankara's security demands and the PKK process.

events.h: Iraqi PM visits Damascus in first such trip since Assad's fall
events.s: Iraqi PM Ali Al-Zaidi met Syrian President Ahmed Al-Sharaa, drawing domestic praise and criticism. Separately, Damascus and Amman gave contradictory accounts of an attack in southern Syria that killed a family.
events.t: Iraq-Syria rapprochement shifts regional alignments around Türkiye's neighbours.

events.h: Pentagon fires Joint Staff planner Sylvia amid Iran war preparations
events.s: Hegseth fired Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, head of strategy and plans on the Joint Staff, reportedly over leaks on Iran and Ukraine, as Trump appears poised to resume large strikes.

events.h: Iran war costs US $47bn as Pentagon eyes $400bn budget cut
events.s: The Pentagon says the Iran war has cost $47bn, days before the midterms. It is also reportedly preparing a $400bn cut to the requested defence budget, which could slow restocking.

events.h: Reuters: Iran imported $2bn in military supplies despite US blockade
events.s: Iran reportedly imported at least $2bn in military supplies since January 2025 through a network of more than 5,000 agencies, despite the US naval blockade.

events.h: Iran repression: executions after January protests, arrests of alleged US-Israel cells
events.s: A UN rapporteur reported at least 34 executions over January protests and thousands detained. Iran separately arrested 16 people it links to US- and Israel-linked cells, and a protester was sentenced to death twice.

events.h: Yemen fighting: heavy casualties, strikes on Houthis and toxic-shell allegations
events.s: WHO says Yemen fighting has killed nearly 1,700 since August. Intensive strikes targeted the Houthis amid suspicions of toxic shells in Taiz, and the Yemeni army claimed 324 Houthis neutralised in 24 hours.

events.h: Abu Dhabi court jails eight for life over arms to Sudan's army
events.s: A UAE court sentenced eight people, including Sudanese army figures Yasser Al Atta and Salah Gosh, to life imprisonment over arms supplies to the Sudanese Army, amid Khartoum-Abu Dhabi tensions.

events.h: Lagarde to leave ECB early as bank holds rates
events.s: Christine Lagarde is resigning effective 7 February, nine months early, opening a succession contest. The ECB held rates despite inflation driven by an energy crisis, and Lagarde signalled a December hike is possible.

events.h: UN envoy Holguin starts new Cyprus talks round
events.s: Maria Angela Holguin will meet Christodoulides on Friday and Turkish Cypriot leader Erhürman on Monday ahead of a tripartite meeting on 9 November.
events.t: Progress on Cyprus interacts with Ankara's maritime dispute with Greece and the Libya deal.

events.h: Türkiye speeds $10bn railway plan for China-Europe freight corridor
events.s: Türkiye is accelerating about $10 billion in rail projects to create a China-Europe freight corridor by 2031, per Nikkei Asia.
events.t: Positions Türkiye as a Middle Corridor transit hub.

events.h: Sinan Ülgen weighs Mecca Alliance benefits and defence risks for Türkiye
events.s: Analyst Sinan Ülgen assessed the Mecca Alliance agreement, its benefits for Türkiye and the risks of its mutual defence obligations.
events.t: The pact's mutual defence clauses could draw Türkiye into Gulf and Iran-related confrontations.

events.h: Russian hybrid threats on NATO flank: sabotage claims, bunkers, conscription
events.s: Reports allege a Russian sabotage and assassination campaign in Europe, with fears of escalation through drone incursions. Estonia plans about 150 border bunkers, Lithuania will introduce conscription for men aged 18-22 from 2032, and NATO reconnaissance flew near Kaliningrad.

events.h: Ukraine reports record Russian losses in October
events.s: Ukraine's General Staff said Russia lost 49,040 troops in October, the highest monthly figure of the full-scale war, and reported strikes on drone and fuel sites in Bryansk.

events.h: Trump administration pushes US firms to take Russian diesel shipments
events.s: Seven tankers with about 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel are sailing to the US under a Trump-Putin deal amid a legal dispute. The administration is privately pressing companies to accept deliveries despite legal risks.

events.h: Hezbollah's Qassem says Iran prioritises ending Israeli attacks on Lebanon
events.s: Naim Qassem said Iran puts ending Israeli attacks and securing Israeli withdrawal first. The Israeli army fired an interceptor at a suspected aerial target in southern Lebanon amid airstrikes.

events.h: Italian EUFOR helicopter crashes in Bosnia, killing at least three
events.s: An EUFOR helicopter crashed in Brcko during an EU mission, with reports of three or four dead and injured.

events.h: IRGC says tankers hit mines or caught fire in Strait of Hormuz
events.s: Iran's IRGC Navy said up to four oil tankers, including a supertanker with over 2 million barrels, were stopped, hit mines or caught fire after using a southern route it called unauthorised. UKMTO said a tanker was struck by explosives attached by a small boat, and Oman rescued 25 crew off Musandam. Analysts note limpet mines are a familiar Iranian tactic, which undercuts US claims that the strait was cleared.
events.t: Disruption in Hormuz pushes energy prices up and raises risk for Türkiye's import bill and regional trade.

events.h: US weighs renewed strikes on Iran after midterms, Gulf states warned
events.s: Reports say Washington told Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense round of strikes on Iran after the November 3 midterms, and Senator Murphy said he was briefed on a plan to restart the war. Netanyahu is reportedly pushing for fresh strikes, while Israeli defence officials doubt a brief air campaign could topple Iran or end its nuclear programme. Axios reports Trump did not discuss strikes with the CENTCOM commander, and Haaretz says the threat is being used as leverage for talks.
events.t: A renewed US-Iran war would hit Türkiye's southern neighbourhood, border security and energy supply.

events.h: Qatari mediators return to Tehran to revive US-Iran deal
events.s: A Qatari delegation led by a senior adviser to the prime minister made its second Tehran visit in a week, holding over 12 hours of talks on a US proposal. Iran International reports Iran rejected an earlier proposal and that the sides are deadlocked over who concedes first. Araghchi says Iran's seven-day plan could be implemented quickly.
events.t: A US-Iran deal would lower regional escalation risk and reduce pressure on Türkiye's energy and border security.

events.h: Vance reportedly offers to meet Iranian security chief Rezaei
events.s: Reports say US Vice President Vance offered to meet Iranian Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei to discuss ending the war. A disclosed letter prompted contradictory narratives in Washington and a conditional response in Tehran. Rezaei is reportedly in contact with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.
events.t: A direct US-Iran channel could open diplomatic room that Ankara has sought to use as a mediator.

events.h: Trump says Iran war will end soon, demands nuclear guarantee
events.s: Trump said in a radio interview that the war will end soon and he expects it wrapped up before the midterms, without giving details. He said the US needs a guarantee Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. Vance said Trump will not let the confrontation become a forever war.

events.h: Oil surges on Hormuz attacks as BP posts record profit
events.s: Oil rose above $114 as traders brace for Iran escalation after the midterms, with Brent over 60 percent above pre-war levels. BP reported its highest profit in about two decades from the Middle East war. Merz says higher energy prices have cost Europe over €100 billion, and EU states agreed to speed the release of 42.6 million barrels from reserves.
events.t: High and volatile energy prices strain Türkiye's inflation and current account, as its central bank noted.

events.h: Zelensky to meet Erdoğan in Istanbul on Black Sea security
events.s: The Turkish presidency said Zelensky will make a working visit to Istanbul on October 31 at Erdoğan's invitation. They will discuss bilateral ties, the war and Black Sea security. Zelensky said the talks come ahead of resumed Ukraine-Russia negotiations next month.
events.t: Ankara reinforces its role as host and mediator in the Ukraine war and Black Sea security.

events.h: US approves $2.1bn sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
events.s: The State Department approved the sale of 500 PAC-3 MSE missiles, to be funded by allies, with no delivery timeline. Zelensky warns deliveries could take years. NATO's SACEUR said third-party transfers and PURL packages are moving forward.

events.h: Kremlin rules out ceasefire ahead of Abu Dhabi trilateral talks
events.s: Russia and the US are coordinating a date for talks in Abu Dhabi, with only mid-November mentioned so far. Peskov said preparations do not require a pause in fighting. Moscow offered a Putin-Zelensky phone call instead of a meeting, which Kyiv suspects is a trap. Lavrov said Russia's position is unchanged.
events.t: Abu Dhabi hosting, rather than Istanbul, shows the diplomatic track is moving to another Muslim-majority venue.

events.h: Ukraine refinery strikes continue amid reported US-pressured pause
events.s: Drones hit the Novokuibyshevsk refinery and Russia says it intercepted over 1,000 drones overnight. Reports say Ukraine paused refinery strikes under US pressure, while a Kremlin aide says Kyiv ignored Trump's request. Russia extended its diesel export ban to January 2027.
events.t: Strikes on Russian energy and Black Sea shipping affect Türkiye's energy and maritime interests.

events.h: Humanitarian ceasefire allows evacuation from occupied Oleshky
events.s: Ukrainian and Russian ombudsmen visited Oleshky during a ceasefire that held for over 80 hours. Evacuees travelled via Crimea, Russia and Belarus, and Russia said its mission was completed. A volunteer alleged some people were moved outside the agreed terms.

events.h: Russian strikes hit Dnipro, Chernihiv, Kremenchuk and Kyiv energy
events.s: A Russian drone strike on a Dnipro train platform killed 15 and Dnipro was hit again, cutting power to over 350,000 customers. Russia launched missiles and over 110 drones overnight, and strikes also hit Chernihiv, Kharkiv and Kyiv infrastructure. Zelensky says Russia took no step toward energy de-escalation.

events.h: Mitsotakis calls Türkiye-Libya maritime deal void, urges Black Sea truce
events.s: Greek PM Mitsotakis called the Turkey-Libya eastern parliament maritime deal blatantly illegal and urged a Black Sea shipping truce. Cyprus repeated at the UN Security Council that the 2019 MoU is null and void.
events.t: The Libya maritime deal underpins Ankara's Eastern Mediterranean claims, and Athens and Nicosia are now contesting it internationally.

events.h: Aliyev skips Ankara Turkic summit amid strained Türkiye-Azerbaijan ties
events.s: Azerbaijani President Aliyev skipped the summit despite a personal invitation, and aides reportedly said it answered Erdoğan skipping a Baku meeting. Erdoğan received Azerbaijan's foreign minister afterward, who spoke on the Middle and Zangezur corridors.
events.t: Open friction with Baku, Ankara's closest ally, threatens the Caucasus corridor agenda.

events.h: Netanyahu's bloc wins 53 seats, no majority; Arab parties surge to 19
events.s: Final results give Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats against 48 for Eisenkot's bloc, with Arab parties nearly doubling to 19. Neither side has 61, and Netanyahu ruled out a government with Arab parties. Talks continue, including Democrats and the United Arab List.
events.t: A weak or unstable Israeli government shapes Israeli behaviour in Syria and Gaza, where Ankara has stakes.

events.h: US orders non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
events.s: The US ordered non-emergency personnel to leave Saudi Arabia, warning of possible attacks on airports. The Saudi-led coalition reports repeated Houthi missiles and drones, including near Riyadh, Jazan and Medina. It said it downed a drone over Mecca, which the Houthis deny.
events.t: Houthi pressure on Saudi Arabia adds to Red Sea and Gulf instability that affects Turkish trade and Gulf partners.

events.h: KCK says peace process with Türkiye has stalled
events.s: KCK spokesperson Sozdar Avesta says the process has stalled and demands a monitoring commission and access to Öcalan.
events.t: A stalled process raises the risk to the effort to end PKK violence, a central Turkish security objective.

events.h: Pakistan's army cautiously optimistic about US-Iran mediation
events.s: Army chief Asim Munir, a chief mediator, visited Tehran twice this month. Pakistan's military is cautiously optimistic about de-escalation but warns of spoilers.

events.h: Washington says Iran cannot pay troops or fund proxies
events.s: Treasury Secretary Bessent says Operation Economic Outcast has left Iran unable to pay troops or fund proxies. A Treasury report says the rial is down about a quarter since August, inflation is near 90%, and no oil has been loaded since August 25.
events.t: Iranian economic collapse could add instability and migration pressure on Türkiye's eastern border.

events.h: US enforces Hormuz blockade as Iran moves hardware past it
events.s: The WSJ reports US forces fly nightly missions to enforce the Hormuz blockade, straining aircraft and crews. Asharq Al-Awsat reports Iran's hidden military agencies are moving hardware past the blockade.

events.h: IRGC claims downing and capture of US drones near Hormuz
events.s: Iran said it destroyed a US unmanned surface vessel and captured a second reconnaissance drone intact, including an MQM-170 near Qeshm Island. CENTCOM denied losing any unmanned vessel, saying all are accounted for. Reports of a hostile fighter jet intercepted over Qeshm are unconfirmed.

events.h: Türkiye nominates Feridun Sinirlioğlu for UN Secretary-General
events.s: Türkiye formally nominated OSCE Secretary General and former foreign minister Feridun Sinirlioğlu after an impasse in Security Council straw polls.
events.t: Ankara bids for the UN's top post, raising its diplomatic profile if the deadlock persists.

events.h: Fidan and Rubio meet at G20 in Atlanta on Iran, Gaza, Ukraine
events.s: Hakan Fidan met Marco Rubio on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers' meeting. They discussed Iran talks, Gaza and the Ukraine war. Fidan also met his Indonesian and Japanese counterparts.
events.t: Direct access to Rubio lets Ankara press its positions on Iran mediation, Gaza and Ukraine.

events.h: G20 family photo cancelled as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
events.s: The US cancelled the G20 foreign ministers' group photo after several European ministers refused to pose with Lavrov. Rubio urged cooperation amid rifts over Ukraine and the Middle East. Lavrov said he held brief but constructive talks with Rubio.
events.t: Ankara, which attends both Western and Russian-inclusive formats, is positioned between the camps.

events.h: Ukraine requests emergency UN Security Council meeting on Russian strikes
events.s: Ukraine's UN envoy requested an emergency session over strikes on Dnipro, Chernihiv and Kremenchuk that killed 20 civilians.

events.h: Ukraine hits Russian Iskander launcher and airfields, expands deep strikes
events.s: Ukraine said it destroyed an Iskander-M launcher in Kursk and struck depots in occupied areas, and imagery reportedly shows two Su-34s destroyed at Marinovka. Zelensky announced expansion of the precision strike zone and long-range units.

events.h: EU Commission proposes €45bn Ukraine funding for 2027
events.s: The Commission proposed disbursing the remaining €45 billion of the €90 billion loan in 2027, with €31.7 billion for defence capacity. Canada pledged €500 million. Euroclear says it has passed €8 billion in frozen-asset proceeds to the Commission, and a Russian court rejected its appeal over a $250 billion ruling.

events.h: Pentagon asks NATO allies to tone down Russia-threat rhetoric
events.s: Four sources say Pentagon officials asked several NATO countries, including Baltic allies, to tone down public rhetoric about the Russian threat.
events.t: A softer US line on Russia would affect NATO threat perceptions on which Ankara's own balancing relies.

events.h: Trump holds off sanctions on Russian fund after prisoner release
events.s: Trump said the US will not lift sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund for now. He praised Russia for securing release of American Hubbard and called new sanctions foolish while he negotiates detainee releases.

events.h: Türkiye and Egypt to hold naval drills amid Eastern Mediterranean tensions
events.s: Asharq Al-Awsat reports Türkiye and Egypt will hold naval drills amid tensions in the Eastern Mediterranean.
events.t: The drills show Ankara-Cairo military rapprochement and add to Eastern Mediterranean signalling.

events.h: Erdoğan hosts 13th Turkic States summit, Ankara Declaration signed
events.s: The Organization of Turkic States summit opened under the theme Turkic Century and adopted a 163-point declaration covering defence, cybersecurity, trade, energy and transport. Erdoğan signed agreements with Uzbekistan and held bilaterals with the Turkmen and Kyrgyz presidents. He called for a Turkic trade, transport and energy hub.
events.t: The summit consolidates Türkiye's leadership in Central Asia and Middle Corridor connectivity.

events.h: Erdoğan and Trump hold two phone calls
events.s: Erdoğan and Trump discussed bilateral ties, Ukraine, the Middle East and the upcoming Turkic states summit in Ankara.
events.t: Frequent leader contact with Trump supports Ankara's bargaining on defence and regional files.

events.h: Erdoğan meets Turkish Cypriot leader as UN envoy Holguin tours Cyprus
events.s: Erdoğan received Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhürman and stressed Turkish Cypriot rights in any settlement. UN envoy Holguin is in Cyprus, plans a tripartite session on November 9 and is optimistic about an enlarged meeting before year's end. Christodoulides says progress is possible.
events.t: Ankara is aligning with Erhürman and defending its two-state-leaning framework as UN diplomacy restarts.

events.h: Netanyahu camp alleges election fraud; Shin Bet probes foreign funding
events.s: Netanyahu's party claimed the vote was stolen and accused Arab parties of taking foreign funding. Election officials rejected the fraud claims, and Shin Bet, with Mossad help, is probing possible Qatari funding. Türkiye denied interfering.
events.t: Ankara is named in Israeli claims of foreign interference, which feeds Israel-Türkiye tension.

events.h: Israeli forces demolish homes in south Lebanon; Qassem says framework void
events.s: Israeli forces demolished homes and shelled towns in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah's Naim Qassem said the US-brokered framework is effectively nonexistent and Hezbollah will keep its weapons while Israel occupies Lebanese land. A Lebanese military court charged 13 over a truck of Hezbollah explosives.

events.h: Israel's Hebron siege displaces thousands as UN warns on Gaza
events.s: Israel declared a Hebron neighbourhood a closed military zone on the eighth day of raids that displaced thousands and demolished gunmen's homes. The UN rights office warns of ethnic cleansing risks in Gaza as Israeli forces treat the Yellow Line as a kill zone. The IDF said it killed Hamas militants in Gaza City strikes.
events.t: Gaza and West Bank escalation sustains Ankara's confrontation with Israel and its diplomatic push on Palestine.

events.h: Houthi missiles hit Aden as Yemeni army claims offensive gains
events.s: Houthi missiles struck Aden's airport and presidential palace, and residents fear a return to full war. Yemen's army says its Dawn of Yemen operation killed 336 Houthis in 1,087 operations. Houthis expanded the Taiz offensive toward Lahj, and the Taiz governor reports siege shortages.

events.h: Iraq integrates Yezidi PKK-linked units in Sinjar; Karayılan endorses
events.s: Baghdad is integrating Yezidi YBŞ units into Iraqi security forces, and PKK's Murat Karayılan endorsed the agreement. Anadolu says it reshapes regional balances.
events.t: Integration of PKK-affiliated units into Iraqi forces touches Ankara's Sinjar concerns and the disarmament process.

events.h: Barrack: Iraq is part of Iran's proxy plans; Baghdad PM takes intelligence control
events.s: US envoy Barrack said Iraq is part of Iran's overall plans, with proxies under ministerial command, and that Iran talks are nearing de-escalation. Separately, Iraq's prime minister took direct control of the intelligence service.
events.t: Iraq's alignment between Washington and Tehran bears on Türkiye's border security and trade routes.

events.h: Turkey's opposition squeezed by CHP ruling and jailed challenger
events.s: Analyses describe an opposition struggling after its presidential challenger was jailed and its main party split by a court ruling. YENİ Parti plans to take the CHP nullity ruling to the ECtHR, and Özgür Özel visited a freed official. Parliamentary resignations cost the Yeni Yol group its status.
events.t: The domestic political contest shapes Erdoğan's room for foreign policy and Europe's view of Türkiye.

events.h: Gulf states rethink defence models as Turkey's drone arsenal draws attention
events.s: Analyses discuss Gulf efforts to bolster defence, including Qatar's domestic weapons and Turkey's drone arsenal. An IISS report argues Gulf states must rethink reliance on US bases after the war. Saudi Arabia and NATO discussed defence cooperation.
events.t: Gulf demand for new suppliers is an opening for the Turkish defence industry.

events.h: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal chief suspended, police deployed
events.s: A judge suspended the court's chief and deputy and took control, and police cordoned off the court. The Tusk-backed move sparked clashes with protesters, and President Nawrocki cut short a Senegal trip.

events.h: Syrian authorities clash with French jihadists as prices soar
events.s: French jihadists clashed with Syrian authorities and accused the government of a three-month siege in a Telegram statement. BBC reports soaring prices after subsidy cuts are testing Ahmed al-Sharaa's government.
events.t: Unrest and jihadist activity in Syria bear on Türkiye's border security and its support for Damascus.

events.h: Turkish intelligence captures suspected ISIL Khorasan operative abroad
events.s: MİT captured a suspected ISIL Afghanistan-branch operative, named as Uğur Bahadır, in the Afghanistan-Pakistan region and brought him to Türkiye.
events.t: The operation shows MİT's reach against ISIL threats to Türkiye.

events.h: Novaya Gazeta announces closure after Russian pressure
events.s: Russia's best-known independent newspaper said it will close after 30 years, citing authorities' pressure and its Moscow office eviction.

events.h: EU and Canada sign trade deal and Alliance for the Future
events.s: The EU and Canada signed a digital trade deal and launched an Alliance for the Future at a Montreal summit as Trump's tariff threats push allies closer. They aim to define a partnership by 2027, with talks possibly concluding in June.

events.h: Dockworkers strike at 113 ports against arms shipments
events.s: Dockworkers at 113 ports in 22 countries struck over arms shipments to wars, including in Türkiye, Greece, Italy and Cyprus.
events.t: Turkish ports took part in the action over arms transfers to Israel.

events.h: Türkiye to host COP31 in Antalya with Lula attending
events.s: Brazil's Lula will attend COP31 in Antalya on November 11-12, and Turkish officials say Türkiye will bridge developed and developing countries on climate action.
events.t: COP31 gives Ankara a prominent multilateral platform.
